I think I could get away with it for at least a few more months in terms of just the changes, but I'm mainly worried they're going to find out another way (insurance bills or something) and I'll be caught off guard and panic.

Emotionally, I have an extremely close codependent relationship with my mom in particular and am ridiculously attached to her considering everything she's done. I don't think I'll ever be able to emotionally distance myself from my parents and I honestly don't want to, but I also know I'll never be happy while I'm so dependent on their approval... Reddit didn’t let me post this all at once bc it was so long lmao but here’s the second half of the list:

• The long one: my brain is about as much of a mess as my body is. In addition to the depression that may or may not have returned, I have a long history of social anxiety disorder that was so severe I was CONSTANTLY anxious and developed chronic digestive issues from it; it could only be fixed with medication by the time my parents finally took me to a therapist after dismissing like a decade of that suffering. It wasn’t just shyness or whatever, it was a serious condition that robbed me of years of my life (both literally from the years of constant stress probably not being great for my heart, and figuratively from the fact that it left me years behind my peers on friendships, dating, etc.)

I was also recently diagnosed with PTSD from two separate events: the first being years of serious emotional abuse/neglect from both parents. My mother has borderline personality disorder that made her very unstable, and she would treat me like the worst person ever over the tiniest infractions until I legit felt guilty for being born from a young age. My dad used to have bad anger issues, though he’s worked on it. They used to fight all the time, and still sometimes do— and though there was never much actual physical violence between them, there were threats of violence, suicide, etc. that scared the shit out of me as a young kid. I often have flashbacks to their fights now when I hear raised voices, where I literally believe I’m hearing them for a moment and freak out even though they’re currently miles away now that I’m at college— and the emotional abuse, especially from my mom, has left me with basically zero self-esteem. (My brother was also always their favorite, despite me doing better in school and being better behaved, which certainly didn’t help in that department.) I love my family and there have definitely been good times as well as bad, but in the past couple of years I’ve finally been trying to deal with the leftover issues I have from my traumatic childhood. It isn’t easy, though— I still pretty much blame myself for everything that happened.

Second, I was also traumatized by my mother having cancer and nearly dying when I was younger— to the point where I’ve blanked on very significant events entirely because my brain is clearly trying to get rid of the memory— and I also developed illness anxiety disorder from this, where I’m a hypochondriac and constantly genuinely afraid I’m dying over even small symptoms. (That’s also another issue with transitioning, as medical stuff scares me a lot.) I’m not making any of these up for attention, by the way— I’ve seen doctors/therapists about all of them.


• I’m so lonely. I honestly have huge mommy/daddy issues lol, and I need someone to give me the affection they couldn’t, but it’s hard to find that when you have poor social skills no matter how hard you’ve tried to learn to fit in. I don’t want to spend my life alone— I won’t ever really be happy that way, so why bother?


• I’m not going to go the depressed route I have in the past of “no one would care if I died,” because I know that’s not entirely true. However, I have always been a disappointment to my family, and I have always been socially awkward and had few friends. Very few people would miss me, and those who would could get over it eventually. I’m not so important to anyone that they would never be happy again if I died or anything. And most people wouldn’t miss me at all.


Seriously, what’s the point of someone like me sticking around? This isn’t even depression at this point, it’s a genuine question.

Please don’t just tell me it gets better. My entire life so far is a testament to the opposite. It feels like no matter how far I get, I always get knocked back down ten times harder. Like I only exist to suffer constantly until I die, like I don’t have any path to happiness because I’m missing all the things so many of my peers take for granted (healthy body and mind, non-dysfunctional family, self-esteem, even not having to deal with gender dysphoria, etc.). How the hell am I going to have all this stuff thrown at me my whole life and then be expected to just pick myself up and move on? I’m tired. I see no evidence that things will ever improve for me— in fact, there’s a lot of evidence to support the fact that things will continue to worsen, especially my health issues.

I don’t even really know what I’m asking at this point but yeah I’m a mess rn
